_about: Field terms for F38, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

stationary.definition: a series whose mean and autocovariance do not change over time
stationary.excludes: series with trends, level shifts or drifting variance

esm.definition: a study design in which people answer short questions on a phone several times a day, so that mood is recorded close to the moment it is felt
esm.excludes: one-off questionnaires and recall of past weeks

surrogate.definition: a simulated series that keeps chosen properties of a real one, here its length, mean, standard deviation and lag-1 memory, and nothing else, so a statistic on the real series can be compared with what those properties alone produce
surrogate.excludes: the real series' distribution of values, which a Gaussian surrogate does not copy

ar1.definition: a series in which each value is the mean plus a fixed fraction of the previous value's distance from the mean, plus fresh random noise
ar1.excludes: steps, drifting coefficients, switching between states and long memory

change-point.definition: a time at which the mean or variance of a series changes; here found by a penalised search that adds a change only when it improves the fit by more than a fixed penalty
change-point.excludes: gradual change, which the drift test reads

drift-test.definition: a comparison of an autoregressive model whose coefficient follows a random walk with one whose coefficient is fixed, by likelihood ratio
drift-test.excludes: a drift of the mean level alone with a constant coefficient, which this test does not target

switching-test.definition: a comparison of a model with two hidden states, each with its own level and spread, that the series moves between, with a single AR(1), by likelihood ratio
switching-test.excludes: a one-way step, which the change-point test reads

ou-time-constant.definition: the time over which a quantity that relaxes toward its mean loses about 63 percent of a deviation, fitted here from each person's prompts at their real times with a separate noise term
ou-time-constant.excludes: a second, slower or faster timescale in the same person, which this fit does not model

sampling-floor.definition: the condition in which a person's fitted time constant is shorter than their median gap between prompts within a day, so the value is not measured
sampling-floor.excludes: a claim that the person's mood is fast; noise gives the same reading

aliasing.definition: the misreading that results when a process changes faster than it is sampled, so that the fast change appears in the record as something else, here as noise
aliasing.excludes: measurement error in the instrument, which is present even with dense sampling

dequantising.definition: adding uniform random noise one scale step wide to values recorded on a coarse scale, so that identical neighbouring answers stop being exactly equal
dequantising.excludes: any recovery of the finer value the person would have given on a continuous scale
